Results.ReviewText:
I have wanted to get into smoking meat for a long time but was always intimidated by the process. I did not want to babysit a fire all night or constantly fiddle with vents. I finally decided to buy the Traeger Ironwood 650 as my very first smoker, and honestly, it makes me look like a professional pitmaster right out of the gate.

If you are a beginner like me and want to know if this investment is worth it, here is my breakdown of the experience.
Construction and Build Quality

Since this was my first unit, I was not sure what to expect regarding assembly and sturdiness. The Ironwood 650 is built like a tank. The legs are thick and stable, and the lid feels heavy and substantial when you open and close it.

The standout feature here is the double side wall insulation. I read that cheaper models leak heat, but this one holds temperature incredibly well. The gasket seals tight, so smoke actually stays inside the chamber where it belongs rather than leaking out the sides. It feels like a high end appliance rather than just a backyard grill.
Temperature Control

This was my biggest worry as a newbie. I had no idea how to manage airflow or fuel. The Ironwood 650 takes all that stress away with the D2 Direct Drive drivetrain. You literally just turn the dial to your desired temperature and hit ignite.

I watched the temperature on the digital display, and it is rock solid. If I set it to 225 degrees, it climbs there quickly and stays there. It recovers heat almost instantly after I open the lid to spritz the meat. It gives me total confidence that I am not going to ruin an expensive cut of meat by letting the heat spike or drop.
Cooking and Flavor

The flavor profile is amazing. I was worried that a pellet grill might not give enough smoke flavor compared to traditional offsets, but the Super Smoke mode solves that. You can toggle this feature on when cooking between 165 and 225 degrees. It forces more smoke over the meat without raising the heat.

My first cook was a brisket, and the results were shocking. It had a beautiful pink smoke ring and a distinct wood fired taste. The meat remained moist and tender. The convection fan circulates the heat and smoke evenly, so I did not even have to rotate the meat during the cook.
Capacity

Do not let the 650 number fool you. This size is perfect for a standard family. I have plenty of room for a full packer brisket and a pork butt at the same time. The grill comes with two porcelain coated racks. The bottom rack is adjustable, which is a great feature. I can lower it to fit a tall turkey or beer can chicken, or keep it higher for steaks and burgers. It strikes the perfect balance of being large enough for a party but not so massive that it takes up my whole patio.

There are two features that saved me during my first few cooks.

1) WiFIRE Technology: Being able to connect the grill to my phone via the Traeger app is incredible. I can sit on my couch and monitor the internal temperature of the meat and the grill temp. I can even change the temperature or turn on Super Smoke from my phone. It makes the long cooks very manageable.

2) Pellet Sensor: As a beginner, I have no idea how fast pellets burn. The built in sensor alerts my phone when the hopper is getting low. This saved me from running out of fuel during an overnight cook.

Conclusion

I am so glad I chose the Ironwood 650 as my first smoker. It removes the learning curve and lets you focus on prepping the food and enjoying the results. The construction is solid, the temperature is precise, and the food tastes incredible. I am officially hooked on smoking.
Results.Title: The perfect entry into smoking for a beginner!

Results.ReviewText:
I have owned my Ironwood 885 for almost 3 years. It is operating as designed with no major issues that many other reviews have mentioned. There have never been any network issues or structural/finish issues (no paint flaking, etc.), and for the most part, no operational issues. I'm just overall underwhelmed with its performance now that I have had opportunities to compare it to other pellet grills of the similar design. (no, I'm not comparing a pellet grill with a true 'stick burner/offset')

I've cooked with true wood burning/smoking prior to getting the Ironwood. The taste and flavour can't really be matched (nor did I expect it to be), however I wanted the ease and automated control of a programmable pellet grill, and “meet in the middle” for 'wood-fired'. This is where it under performs. As far as the technology and automatic control goes, it does the job. However, there is very little actual 'wood-fried’ flavour and I have now spent a few years trying different temperatures, different pellet fuel (yes Traeger brand pellets as well), "super-smoke" mode (which makes little to no difference), and varying timeframes to no avail. Sure, I can add an aftermarket 'smoke tube' to burn in the chamber to add smoke flavour, but doesn't that defeat the purpose of a pellet grill/smoker?? It now becomes an expensive outdoor oven with a smoke tube. This is where I’m at however, and, shouldn’t be the case.

Lastly, the temperature sensor/control of the cooking chamber has never been accurate, on average running about 20C lower than the display reads. There is a calibration for the temperature probes, but none for the built-in sensor. Using numerous secondary thermometers (INLCUDING a Meater Probe owned by Traeger themselves) The temperature on those thermometers is 20C lower than then Ironwood says. Hence, you must set and run the Ironwood at approx. 20C higher to get the chamber temperature you desire. This is especially problematic if you want to run at 225C (the maximum temp Super Smoke will work) but have to set it at 245C in order to get real-world 225C. Setting it at 245C disables Super Smoke, while on the other end, if you set it at 225C the real-world temp is about 200C, resulting in increasing cooking times significantly. So yes, while it is functional, it's problematic, and after researching online there is no known fix (it’s long out of warranty but has been a consistent problem since day one.) 

All in all, I enjoy the look, build, and finish of the unit. It's well-built, just quite underwhelming in performance when compared to the same cooks side-by-side with a close competitor, Reqtec. For the high price, I would say it’s below-average, and would not buy Traeger again. Evaluated against a friend's dozens and dozens of cooks over the same time period, side by side on his Reqtec 700, if I had to do it again I would buy a Reqtec which is of similar build quality, wifi technology, achieves closer to a true wood fired smoker and, with accurate temps. Unfortunately, I'm not going to recoup the money spent in reselling the Ironwood, in order for me to switch at this point.

ClientResponses.Response: Hello, and thanks for your feedback on the Ironwood 885. Whenever WiFIRE grills like the Ironwood 885 shutoff in the middle of a cook, it is almost always due to a few limited causes. Assuming that it is not simply the result of a GFI outlet or a breaker tripping, there is a good chance that either the grill’s firmware, or the app, is not up to date. To verify this, information for both is available at traeger.com/status, though they should update automatically as long as phone updates aren't turned off and the grill is regularly left in standby mode (leave switch in the on position at the back of the hopper). Another possibility could be a damaged or loosely connected wire, including the power cord, which plugs into the convertor under the pellet hopper (just remember to unplug the cord from the wall before checking any wires). However, there is really no need to do anything by yourself since you can access Traeger Customer Service 365 days a year for assistance. Before attempting another overnight cook, please consider reaching out to us first, and we will go over everything discussed here, and even some less likely possibilities as well.
ClientResponses.Name: Traeger Grills

ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thanks for your review of the Ironwood 885. Although regularly cleaning your pellet grill is certainly a good approach for any outdoor cooker, if your Ironwood is shutting down like this, then whatever the cause is should be correctable. One thing that may be related is the bottom of the pellet hopper, where the auger opening is. While basic maintenance mostly deals with the inside of the barrel, it is important to make sure that wood dust is not accumulating in the hopper, as this can interfere with pellet flow and cause problems with the temperature. You might also want to make sure that the grill is going through the complete startup process, which simply involves waiting for the grill to reach your set temperature, with the lid closed and no food inside. But if everything discussed here is already being done, please consider reaching out to Traeger Customer Service so that one of our agents can check over your grill with you, and possibly even do a test run to determine what is causing the unusual behavior from your Ironwood.

ClientResponses.Response: Hello, and thanks for your review of the Ironwood 885. If you are getting an Ignitor (or Hot Rod) Disconnected error, it is often simply due to the connection coming loose on the back of the controller, though it may also mean the ignitor needs to be replaced. You can check the hot rod wire by disconnecting the grill from the power outlet, removing the four screws on the control panel, and making sure that the plug with the double, candy cane colored wires (white, with red stripe) is firmly attached to the back of the controller. As an extra step, you can also try carefully unplugging each component (the four multiwire plugs on the left side, including the hot rod plug) from the controller and securely plugging it back in again, then trying the grill once everything is put back and the power cord is back in the outlet. Although this is a fairly straightforward process, you may feel more comfortable with an agent on the line when you do it. To avoid busier times for our Customer Service Team, you can check the estimated wait at the bottom right of support.traeger.com, which is also the same page where we have our phone number (bottom left) and chat link (orange circle with chat icon at bottom right corner).

ClientResponses.Response: Hello, and thank you for your feedback on the Ironwood 885. Power issues on WiFIRE grills are pretty straight forward once you know what to look for, but it is always going to be much easier with someone from Traeger Customer Service helping you. While there are a few quick steps that you can try on your own, based on your comments, most of them may have been done already. But since you're sure that the outlet it is ok, you might also check the power cord to make sure it is not damaged, and most importantly, that it is securely plugged in to the power converter at the bottom of the hopper. This is one of the most common causes of a WiFIRE grill not getting power, and the simplest to fix (just push it up firmly into the converter box). Although there are several other possibilities that can be checked, with more in-depth steps found in the “D2 Controller Display Not Turning On” article on support.traeger.com, it will likely be much easier with someone from Customer Service on the line with you. To make this process as convenient as possible, our support line is open seven days a week, up until 10:00 PM MT. You can also avoid hold times by checking the wait estimate that is available at the bottom right of the Traeger support site pages.

Results.ReviewText: I upgraded to an Ironwood Series about 2 years back.  I have used it 12-15 times to this point.  I keep it clean, it is covered on a patio, and has a Traeger cover I bought to protect it.  I have had issues with it maintaining temperature since I have had it, but being an experienced (I own a Weber Smokey Mountain/Kamado Joe/Cook Shack) smoker, I understand it isn't ceramic/insulated and just adjust the temp higher as necessary to maintain internal temps.  No biggie, I can work around that even with the 1500 price tag.  But what I can't, is the internal electronics.  I tried to fire it up recently (after not using it for a couple months) and I get no power.  Tested the outlet and it works fine.  No water, it is completely dry internally being under cover.  No insects or other issues that would interfere.  I read through the "Support" and have tired chat and calling.  I was left on hold a couple times for longer than I could wait, and the chat rep never responded in the chat.  I am hoping this review will get me some response.  At this point, I can't be an advocate for the Ironwood Grill.  I hope support can change my mind.  If anyone reads this, please contact me.

ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thank you for your feedback on the Ironwood 650. As you have correctly stated, the MEATER Block does not directly link to the Ironwood 650. This model, as well as the Ironwood 885, was in production a while before Traeger acquired MEATER, so there is no functionality in the existing controller software to pair them with the probes. Additionally, this version of the MEATER probe does not directly connect with any grill, even the new touchscreen Ironwood, Ironwood XL, Timberline or Timberline XL. For these latest versions of the Ironwood and Timberline, there is the X MEATER, which was developed in tandem with the Traeger touchscreen models to provide cook data right in the Traeger app. But in your particular case, the wireless Bluetooth MEATER Block would actually be the appropriate probes for your Ironwood 650 (or just about any other grill) and can be used with the MEATER app on most Android and Apple smartphones. However, if you are certain that you paid $400 for the probes, and purchased them through Traeger.com, please reach out to Customer Service, as this would be a substantial (though unusual) overcharge that we would be happy to correct.
ClientResponses.Name: Traeger Grills

ClientResponses.Response: Thank you for your review of the Ironwood 885. Smoking temps range from 165-225, and the super smoke option can be used in this temp range. To get more of a smoke flavor, we would recommend smoking on a lower temp for a longer period of time. Make sure to use your meat probe to Cook to the meats internal temperature. Putting the meat on the top rack can also help. Different pellets also have different levels of smoke flavor, for example hickory will be stronger than oak or alder and cherry would have less of a smoke flavor. You can learn more about smoke and pellets on our support site. You can also find the grill guide that has useful information for your Ironwood 885.
ClientResponses.Name: Traeger Grills

Results.ReviewText:
The good: maintains stable temp

The bad: little to no smoke flavor. Only able to use super smoke <225 even at that minimal smoke flavor. 

First cook:  18lb brisket, very tender and juicy. 885 regulated the temp very well. Confirmed internal temp with electric oven thermometer and an analog oven therm. But it had almost zerrrro smoke flavor. 

2nd cook: 4 racks baby back. Added smoke tube and ran first hour at 225 super smoke. Better smoke flavor but still not enough for spending 1300$ traeger. 

3rd cook: poor man burnt ends and 2 St. Louis ribs. 1 smoke tube. Same as 2nd cook. 

I ordered a second smoke tube and feel that will solve my complaint of no smoke flavor. But traeger sells this as a “smoker” so I am disappointed to spend 1300$ and need to use 2 smoke tubes. 

Previous smoker was a pitboss, it smoked much better but had massive temp swings. So overall I do like the traeger better due to stable temps. But it is also almost 3x price of my old pitboss.
